newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse ranks first among emerging mkts - IFC.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse ranks first among emerging mkts - IFC.

text.p: Greece's stock exchange is the best performer among 45 emerging markets with a year-to-date return of 38.7 percent in dollar based on IFC's investable total return indexes, said IFC.

"The Athens stock exchange is the best performing emerging market as covered by the IFC's Investable Total Return Indexes, with a year-to-date performance of 38.7 percent in US dollars," it said in a flash report.
Return calculations were based on closing prices of April 23. The Athens stock exchange general index advanced another 0.54 percent to 1,464.75 points on Tuesday.

Falling inflation and interest rates, a shift from fixed income to equities, good corporate results, increased interest from emerging market funds for all European emerging stock markets account for the continuation of the rally, it said.

The privatisation of state-owned firms, recent corporate actions in the banking sector, the government's dedication for a more transparent market and a new code of conduct of trading rules provide reasons for sustaining the Athens bourse's rally.

"It is worth noting that even though the IFC Investable Index P/E ratio for Greece significantly increased after the recent stock rally, 15.94 x, it is still well below its all-time high of 36.73x," it said.
The Greek stock exchange's P/E ratio is one of the lowest in Europe and among the 45 emerging markets covered by the IFC, said the report written by head market analyst Constantinos Grigoriadis.

The Athens bourse still tops all 45 emerging markets with a market dividend yield of 3.95 percent and ranks third with a market capitalisation of $30.4 billion behind Russia with $67.5 billion and Turkey $43.7 billion, it added.
